Chart-16.2: 16.7.1 Investigation of cases and suspects is primarily done by the Subordinate Civil Police Officers (from the rank of an A.S.I. to an Inspector). So, it will be appropriate to analyse the load of work on Investigating Officers instead of working it on all Policemen. The ratio of the strength of the Investigating Officers to the total IPC crimes (1,15,993:21,66,618) to be investigated (cases pending from previous year:4,57,042 and cases reported during 1996:17,09,576), acts as a somewhat balanced indicator of the work load on the Investigating Officers. In the absence of separate strength of police officers earmarked for investigation purposes, if, it is assumed that the entire existing strength (1,15,993) from the level of an A.S.I. to an Inspector (of Civil Police) had been exclusively pressed into the task of investigation of IPC cases only (leaving aside the cases under Special and Local Laws, for the time being), the All-India work load for an Investigating Officer worked out to be 18.7 cases per I.O. during 1996. The work-load of IPC cases was the highest (54.8) in D&N Haveli followed by Madhya Pradesh (44.7), Kerala (43.7) and Gujarat (43.6).
